source_review.notes: Checked NIST SP 800-162 ABAC definition and 2019 update; OWASP API Security Top 10 2023 object- and function-level authorization guidance; RFC 9110 denial/concealment semantics; the primary 2019 Zanzibar paper; and foundational RBAC and complete-mediation literature.

evidence: Reviewed decision function, authorized collection set, effect/version binding, privilege inputs, and non-bypass property notation.
notation_and_syntax.notes: All symbols are introduced and TeX remains inside GitHub-supported delimiters.

evidence: Executed six deterministic policy cases covering permit, relationship denial, tenant denial, field denial, state denial, and policy indeterminate.
numerical_recomputation.notes: Each case reaches the first intended policy boundary and matches exact output.

evidence: Checked conjunction of subject/action/object/environment/policy, authorized-set filtering before pagination, and same-version permit/effect requirement.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: Permit validity is explicitly scoped to policy-relevant inputs and consistency.

evidence: Reviewed wrong object, tenant, parent, relationship, field, state, stale version, hidden count, batch item, policy outage, cache revocation, graph consistency, downstream service, queued work, break-glass, and concealment side channels.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Function, object, tenant, relationship, field, state, temporal, operational, and disclosure boundaries are separated.

evidence: Checked default deny, exact object mediation, tenant scoping, write allowlists, read projections, authorized collection semantics, check/effect consistency, reauthorization, obligation enforcement, cache dependencies, and no effects on deny/indeterminate.
invariant_checking.notes: Authentication and opaque identifiers are never treated as authorization.

proof_review.notes: No formal proof of arbitrary policy correctness or distributed enforcement is claimed.

proof_sketch_labeling.notes: No proof sketch is claimed; equations define local policy and enforcement obligations.

evidence: The executable model explicitly disclaims policy-engine, database-consistency, and system evidence; Zanzibar scale claims are attributed only to the published system; unit, differential, concurrency, and operational tests receive bounded claims.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: Recorded decisions are not presented as proof that enforcement occurred.

conceptual_review.notes: Reviewed authorization tuple, function/object mediation, target identifiers, tenant binding, RBAC/ABAC/ACL/ReBAC/capability choices, PDP/PEP, effect consistency, field reads/writes, collections, graph relationships, concealment, bulk/asynchronous work, caching, obligations, failure, audit, and testing.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed BOLA/function bypasses, tenant and nested-resource attacks, mass assignment, filter/count leakage, TOCTOU, remote PDP failure, policy cache revocation, graph consistency, queued effects, downstream enforcement, break-glass, and safe denial telemetry.

pedagogical_review.notes: Reviewed one-page retrieval, one executable six-case decision audit, ten distinct worked examples, and five exercises progressing from check identification through concurrency tracing, diagnosis, architecture comparison, and asynchronous bulk transfer.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external academic or practitioner review is claimed.
